title: Show HN: Ts-chef – CyberChef-style data transformations inside VS Code
text:
Hi HN,

I've been working on ts-chef, an open-source VS Code extension that brings CyberChef-style data transformations and analysis directly into the editor.

The idea came from a simple workflow problem: when working with encoded data, logs, suspicious scripts, or binary formats, I often found myself switching between my editor and external tools just to decode something, inspect it, or apply a sequence of transformations.

ts-chef tries to make that workflow more convenient.

It currently includes 479 registered operations covering encoding, decoding, hashing, encryption, compression, structured data, and various binary formats.

Some of the features include:

- Visual recipe editor with branching pipelines and multiple outputs - Automatic detection and decoding previews for encoded values on hover - Pattern scanning for Base64, hex, JWTs, hashes, URLs, and other formats - Recursive analysis of layered encodings - Static malware triage, YARA scanning, and entropy visualization - Reusable pipelines, configurable keyboard shortcuts, and operation history

The core transformations run locally without requiring an account or external service. Network-dependent operations are only executed when explicitly selected.

The project is written in TypeScript, licensed under Apache 2.0, and includes operations ported from GCHQ's CyberChef.

I'm not trying to replace CyberChef. My goal is to make these kinds of transformations and analysis workflows accessible where developers and security researchers already spend much of their time.

I'd be interested in feedback, particularly from people working in reverse engineering, security research, or debugging who regularly deal with encoded or structured data.

GitHub: https://github.com/MichaelWeissDEV/ts-chef
